anomalies.observed: C4 (2u2) has one terminal on the node shared with D1 and R3, and its other terminal is tied to a GND symbol. It does not appear to connect to REG_SW, the switch node that the MIC26903 bootstrap capacitor requires.
anomalies.expected: The MIC26903 bootstrap capacitor should sit between BST and SW, with the bootstrap diode feeding BST from the 5 V supply. Its lower terminal should be the switch node, not ground.

evidence.quote: C4 2u2 with GND symbol beneath it, next to D1 SD103AWS and R3 10k (Power sheet, page 1)
REG1 MIC26903YJL-TR, BST pin 20 labelled REG_BST and SW_6/SW pins labelled REG_SW (Power sheet, page 1)
A MIC26903YJL-TR synchronous buck regulator steps the battery input down to 5 V.

anomalies.impact: If C4 is really tied to GND, the high-side gate drive for the buck switch cannot be generated, so the 5 V regulator would fail to switch or would run poorly. I am not certain of the wire routing at this scale, so this is a low-confidence finding.
